I am 55 this year. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and do some figuring, but mostly I go by what I have done before and what the neighbors are doing. My wife works in a garment factory in town, so it is mostly just me on our 10.1 mu here in Quzhou. We have a well, so I can pump water when the rain is not enough, but electricity costs money, so I count every time I start the pump.

I keep 8 mu for wheat and then maize, and 2.1 mu for cotton. I cannot handle more cotton because hand-picking takes too much labor, and my wife is only free on Sundays. 

For the wheat that is already in the ground since last October, I sowed an improved variety — Jimai 22 — because Old Wang next door planted it last year and got a good harvest. Before sowing I spread 100 jin per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer. Now in spring I top-dress twice: 50 jin per mu of urea at green-up, and another 50 jin per mu at jointing. I figured it out from the bag labels: that comes to about 22 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Last year I did almost the same and got about 450 kg per mu, so I will not change it. I will irrigate four times — green-up now, jointing, heading, and grain filling — because losing yield is worse than paying for pump electricity. I will spray three times: herbicide when it warms up, fungicide if rust shows, and insecticide if aphids come. Last autumn I rotavated the field before sowing.

For summer maize on the same 8 mu, I will plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in early June — I buy it from the dealer in town and have used the same kind for three years. At planting I put 80 jin per mu of compound fertilizer in the rows, and at big-flare stage I top-dress with 80 jin per mu of urea. That works out to about 18 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: after planting, at jointing, and at filling. I spray twice — herbicide at planting and insecticide for corn borer in July. I use the no-till planter behind the combine; no extra tillage, saves diesel and time. I expect 550 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For cotton, I plant hybrid seed in late April. I rotary till the 2.1 mu first to warm the soil. Base fertilizer is 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer. Then I top-dress twice with urea, 60 jin per mu each time, and at flowering I add 30 jin per mu of potassium sulfate because the dealer said it helps boll setting and I saw it work on Liu's plot last year. Total is about 18 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate four times: at planting, budding, flowering, and boll stage. Pesticides I spray four times because aphids and mites always show up, plus whatever worms the Bt seed does not stop. I hope for 280 kg per mu of seed cotton.

Fertilizer prices went up again this spring. It hurts. But I remember 2013 when I tried to save 20 yuan per mu on urea and the wheat turned yellow — I lost almost 100 kg per mu. Never again. I would rather spend a bit more than risk a bad harvest. We only have two of us in the house, but every yuan matters, and if I spend too much on fertilizer I have less for pesticide. So I watch what I do and copy the neighbors who always seem to do well.
